🚨🇲🇽 <u>Declassified: the CIA war-gamed invading Mexico in 1989</u>

Newly surfaced CIA documents from May 1989 show Washington ran the numbers on Mexico: an 80% bet that Salinas would hold power, a 20% chance of collapse — and in that case, the agency wrote, "a unilateral military intervention would only be considered in the extremely improbable case that political system collapse was imminent." The same files praise Salinas, the "ambitious technocrat" who privatized some 400 state enterprises after the fraudulent 1988 election. Empire's affection for a neoliberal, and its contingency plan for everyone else.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico slashes the red tape choking its small businesses</u>

Sheinbaum's new package lets small firms pay 7% VAT instead of 15%, cuts the IMSS registration form from 80 fields to 14, collapses eight bureaucratic procedures into one, and drops the wait from 20 days to five. Micro-businesses earning up to 5 million pesos get their income-tax exemption raised to 1 million and can pay quarterly — reaching an estimated 18,000 firms. Formalizing the economy by making it easier, not by punishing the small.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico has the lowest unemployment in the developed world</u>

While the OECD average sat at 4.9% in July, Mexico closed the month at 2.9% — one of only three member economies under 3%, alongside Japan and South Korea. Spain limped in at 10%, Finland at 10.5%. The "failed state" the US press keeps inventing has more of its people in work than almost anywhere on Earth.

🇲🇽🛢️ Pemex was the neoliberals' "petty cash." "They said they had responsible finances because their deficit was tiny. But who did they pile the debt onto? Pemex — with no results, just to prop up public spending. That's the truth." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Under Peña Nieto, Pemex debt climbed from $64 billion to $113 billion. This government cut it by $20 billion and says Pemex needs almost no federal support in 2027.

🇲🇽✊ "Where did they cut? In health, in education." "In the neoliberal era, health and education were exactly where they cut. The so-called 'austerity' never touched top officials' salaries or the money handed to the media." — President Claudia Sheinbaum She set that record against the 2027 budget: education +10.7%, science +13%, health +11.3%. The gap between the richest and poorest tenth fell from 34x in 2008 to 16x in 2024.

🇲🇽🌎 Sheinbaum draws the red line in the USMCA talks. "Let the people of Mexico know: we will not sign anything that harms our sovereignty or our economy. What we're seeking are better trade terms." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the U.S. trade negotiations Mexico is pressing Washington to cut steel, aluminum and auto tariffs and add no new ones, while refusing to trade away sovereignty on the 54 "non-tariff barriers" on the table.
